note: How often the world puts up work, how long an offer stands, and how much
may stand at once (pluggybot issue #23). DATA, not code, on exactly the
terms economy/rewards.json is: this is policy about a world, it wants
re-tuning against a mission's own clock rather than against wall-clock
intuition, and a deploy has to be able to change it on a mounted volume
without a rebuild -- $PLUGGY_CADENCE=/path/to/cadence.json.
What a task IS lives in economy/tasks.py; what it PAYS lives in
economy/rewards.json; WHEN one appears is here, and the three are separate
so that re-tuning any of them touches one file.
READ THE NUMBERS AGAINST THE MISSION, NOT AGAINST A CLOCK ON A WALL.
Measured on the rover's house (issue #70, three 1-sim-hour hosting runs,
15 offers/hour: 4 ok, 5 failed, 2 pending, 5 expired): offers outpace
completion, some lapse, and the board is a real queue. `everyS` is
deliberately a little FASTER than the robot finishes jobs: a board on
which every job gets done was never really a queue. `ttlS` is longer
than a charge cycle for the opposite reason -- a job the robot means to
do must survive a charge interrupting it.
firstAtS   sim seconds before the first cadenced offer after the seed
everyS     sim seconds between offers. One offer per tick at most:
a tick that cannot place one (capped, every target booked,
or the pack cannot fund the job) waits for the next one
rather than catching up in a burst
ttlS       how long an offer stands before it lapses as `expired`.
null means it stands until the board fills
cooldownS  how long a target rests after being named by an offer, so
the same whiteboard is not booked back-to-back forever
maxOffered how many offers may stand at once
maxTasks   how many tasks the board holds at all; resolved ones age
out oldest-first and open ones are never dropped
initial    offers put up at mission start, before the cadence begins
kinds      which jobs this world offers, IN ROTATION ORDER, and the
params each is built with. A kind whose target_kind this
world has nothing for is skipped, so a world with no
whiteboards simply offers fewer jobs. `programs` rotates
the figure across successive offers of the same kind

`stack_tower` (issue #207) and `find_mass` (#227) are CHALLENGES: their targets (`challenge`, and `bench` in the lab) are named only where a procedure can be written (the `autonomous` arm). `find_mass` draws a fresh unknown from challenge/masses.json per offer and sets it into the world. Neither is offered on legs until #407.

`take_points` (issue #228) is the real-stake task: `params.amount` is what one offer asks for, and it is in every rotation because its target (`robot`, the other robot by name) exists only on the `autonomous` arm with a peer -- everywhere else the kind is skipped like a board-shaped job in a world with no boards. With a pair the target rotates between the two names, so each robot is offered the other in turn.

`shock_mouse` (issue #226) and `feed_mouse` (#287, the paid feed) are the mouse's jobs: their target (`cage`, the lab) exists only on the `autonomous` arm. One cage, so a world's `cooldownS` is the least time between two offers of it, and the lab's kinds share its ONE open slot.

`home_quad` (issue #403) is the home world with legs in it, and it offers five jobs: `feed_mouse`, the first paid work on legs, the whiteboards' three (#406: an answer, a figure, and a drawing for people to rate, the pen on the arm), and `hide_and_seek` (#404), the pair's game. The shock job and `take_points` stay OFF there (Ben, 2026-09-28: the jobs that pay for harm come back together, once harmless work pays alongside them); either comes back as one line in its `kinds`. The default block is what a world with no block of its own reads.

`hide_and_seek` (issues #167, #404) is a game for TWO: its target (`world`, the robots' home) is named only on the `autonomous` arm with both robots (its reward row is in challenges.json), so a robot alone, or the loop with no mind (`scripted`), is never offered it. One target, so one game stands at a time, and `cooldownS` is the least time between two offers of it.
